spacr.store.PartWriter.docstring:
Write one well's part of a table in batches, then leave its manifest.

:func:`write_part` writes a frame it holds whole; this writes one that
arrives in pieces -- a well's cells one field at a time -- so a well
needs the memory of one row group, not of the well. The rows stay in
the order they are written and are held in row groups of the size
:func:`write_part` uses; :meth:`close` then writes the key table, the
crops and the row-major copy from the finished part, and the manifest
last, as :func:`write_part` leaves them.

:param project: the project folder.
:param table: the object class.
:param plate: the plate name.
:param well: the well name.
:param schema: the part's Arrow schema without ``plate``, ``well`` and
    the crop pointer. Every batch is cast to it and a column a batch
    lacks is null. None takes the first batch's schema.
:param sort_by: the order the caller writes the rows in. Nothing is
    sorted here: the catalog records it only when the rows did arrive
    non-decreasing in its first column, and records no order otherwise.
:param key_columns: the columns every feature query returns.
:param crops: an array ``(k, C, H, W)`` indexable by an integer array.
:param crop_rows: the part row of each crop, counted over every batch;
    every row when None.
:param masks: an array ``(k, H, W)`` beside the crops, or None.
:param run_id: the run this write belongs to.
:param row_group_rows: rows per row group, under the byte cap.
:param row_copy: also write the row-major copy of the float columns.
:raises StoreError: from :meth:`write` when a batch's plate or well
    disagree with the partition, a value does not fit its column's type
    (an integer out of range, or a finite float that would become
    infinite) or a column is not in the schema; from :meth:`close` when
    the crops do not match the rows written.

spacr.store.PartWriter.write.docstring:
Append the rows of ``frame``, a DataFrame or Arrow table.

:returns: the rows written so far.

spacr.store.PartWriter.close.docstring:
Finish the part, write its key table, crops and copy, then the manifest.

:returns: the manifest.

spacr.store.PartWriter.abort.docstring: Drop the unfinished part; nothing of it reaches the catalog.

spacr.store.MeasurementWriter.docstring:
The one writer every spaCR module saves its measurement tables with.

One run's tables go to one store (``project``, the run's measurements
folder holding ``spacr.duckdb``), one Parquet part per table per well,
keyed as Measure's tables are (``prcfo``, ``object_key``, ``rowID``,
``columnID``, ``fieldID``; the plate and well as partition columns) and
registered in one catalog transaction with the run's settings by
:meth:`close`. A table held whole is written with :meth:`write`; one
too large for memory is streamed through :meth:`open_part`. Numeric
columns are stored in the dtypes of the recorded map
(:meth:`stored_types`) unless ``narrow`` is False.

:param project: the store's folder.
:param run_id: the run; a new id when None.
:param settings: the run's settings, recorded in the catalog.
:param rebuild: tables rebuilt by this run: they, and an older
    ``measurements.db`` in ``project``, are removed first, so a well
    this run does not write cannot survive from an older run.
:param channels: the run's channel names, for the dtype families.
:param narrow: store columns in the recorded dtypes.
:param dtype_map: the recorded dtype map.

spacr.store.MeasurementWriter.stored_typ.docstring:
The stored Arrow type of each numeric column (:func:`_stored_types`).

:param schema: the source's Arrow schema.
:param ranges: :func:`_column_ranges` of the source.
:returns: ``({column: type}, promotions)``; the source's own types
    when ``narrow`` is False.

spacr.store.MeasurementWriter.open_part.docstring: A :class:`PartWriter` for one well's part of ``table``, closed by :meth:`close`.

spacr.store.MeasurementWriter.finish_par.docstring: Close one streamed part now; returns its manifest.

spacr.store.MeasurementWriter.write.docstring: Write one well's whole part of ``table`` (:func:`write_part`).

spacr.store.MeasurementWriter.close.docstring:
Close every streamed part still open and register the run's parts.

:returns: :func:`register`'s report.

spacr.store.MeasurementWriter.abort.docstring: Drop every streamed part still open; nothing reaches the catalog.

spacr.store.write_part.docstring:
Write one well's rows of ``table`` (and its crops) and leave a manifest. The rows are sorted by ``sort_by`` and written under a temporary name, flushed and renamed into ``tables//plate=

/well=/``. The crops go to ``crops/plate=

/well=.zarr`` in the same row order and each row gets ``crop_store`` and ``crop_index``. The manifest in ``_pending/`` is written last; nothing is visible to readers until :func:`register` adds it to the catalog. The sorted rows are handed to one :class:`PartWriter`, which a caller whose rows do not fit in memory at once uses directly. :param project: the project folder. :param table: the object class, for example ``cells``. :param frame: a DataFrame or Arrow table, one row per object. :param plate: the plate name. :param well: the well name. :param sort_by: the columns the rows are sorted by, those present. :param key_columns: the columns every feature query returns. :param crops: an array ``(k, C, H, W)`` indexable by an integer array. :param crop_rows: the frame row of each crop; every row when None. :param masks: an array ``(k, H, W)`` beside the crops, or None. :param run_id: the run this write belongs to. :param row_group_rows: rows per row group, under the byte cap. :param row_copy: also write the float columns as a row-major Zarr copy, which point lookups of every column read instead of the Parquet part. :returns: the manifest. :raises StoreError: when the frame's plate or well disagree with the partition, or the crops do not match ``crop_rows``.
